question.title: Design a Log System
question.shortDescription: Design a logging system that stores timestamped messages and supports time-range queries

followUpQuestions.questionText: What is the time complexity of your solution for both storing and retrieving logs?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Expected answer:
• Store: O(1) - just append to list/array
• Retrieve: O(n) for linear scan, or O(log n + k) for binary search where k = results

Strong candidates:
• Explain trade-offs between different approaches
• Mention binary search optimization

followUpQuestions.questionText: How would you optimize this if retrieveLogs is called much more frequently than storeLog?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Look for:
• Binary search for finding range boundaries
• Indexing strategies (by hour/day for faster lookup)
• Caching frequent queries

Advanced:
• Segment tree or interval tree for complex queries
• Time-based indexing/bucketing

followUpQuestions.questionText: What if logs don't arrive in chronological order? How would you modify your solution?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Should discuss:
• Need to sort logs (adds O(n log n) complexity)
• Using a sorted data structure (TreeMap, heap)
• Trade-offs in insertion vs retrieval performance

Bonus:
• Buffering and periodic sorting
• Maintaining sorted invariant

followUpQuestions.questionText: How would you extend this to support filtering by log level (INFO, WARN, ERROR)?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Good answers include:
• Add level field to log entries
• Multiple indexes (one per level)
• Composite filtering in retrieve method
• Hash map of level -> logs

Shows:
• Understanding of multi-dimensional indexing
• Design extensibility thinking
